item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I'm not a fan of the excessive expungements. Additionally, redacting percentages strikes me as a little silly, especially when given the first digit and the phrase "over 90%" would give me the same idea. Furthermore, redacting what millennium an event takes place in makes it fairly useless. The one that takes place in February for instance takes place on a commuter train. That mean it could easily be in 1XXX or 2XXX without risking much. I'd even say 19XX or 20XX still leaves it vague enough for the Foundation's purposes and it would also be realistic from a reader's perspective that the actual year would be classified. -1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I love the take on fungus and the common cold. The idea of several chained infections each one leading to another is really cool. The only issues I have is that the percent of immune people is too low as 2% of the world population is still a huge number of people. The other issue is that the pointless redactions take me out of the story. It wasn't super noticeable until the "9█% chance of becoming infected" line. What reason is there to keep the exact infection rate hidden but still tell me its at least 90%. After seeing this the rest of the pointless redactions became a lot more noticable.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There's one thing I still don't understand: Why is some kind of dangerous parasite/disease that's widespread like this considered an anomaly? While I understand how scary it might be for a person to be eaten from inside by some pathogens, it still exists and Nothing about it makes it anomalous.
Does it come out of thin air? Does it do something impossible to do by normal physics or biology etc. ? Does it act in anyway to consider it part of foundation's job to suppress it?
If no then it's just a non anomalous albeit dangerous disease or parasite.

I can't come up with any justification at all for ANY of the expungements or black boxes in this article.

Also:

In the event of Stage Four or Stage Five outbreak, in addition to the above procedures, [DATA EXPUNGED], as described in Document #129-A-2 (Level 4 clearance required).

Aside from the cardinal sin of an expungement in the containment procedures, a lesser (but still annoying) issue is that's not what [DATA EXPUNGED] means. If the information is available in Document #129-A-2, then it hasn't been [DATA EXPUNGED], merely [REDACTED].

Hmmmmmm. Looking into this skip, I am reminded a lot of SCP-1627 due to both being fungal infections with similar means of infecting. That SCP-129's effects are highly variable in the later stages, its not too far gone for someone to consider SCP-1627 to possibly be an offshoot of SCP-129. Recommending the addition of the following edits:

Changing this:

Due to a combination of historical events, most humans and animals are naturally immune to SCP-129-04 through SCP-129-██. Therefore, outbreaks of Stage Three infections are quite rare, but have the potential for widespread infection if not swiftly isolated and contained. All known cases of SCP-129 have followed the below five-stage progression, although [DATA EXPUNGED], possibly due to mutation.

To this:

Due to a combination of historical events, most humans and animals are naturally immune to SCP-129-04 through SCP-129-██. Therefore, outbreaks of Stage Three infections are quite rare, but have the potential for widespread infection if not swiftly isolated and contained. All known cases of SCP-129 have followed the below five-stage progression, although [DATA EXPUNGED], possibly due to mutation.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Also, this may just be me, but it seems like, as written, there really isn't anything substantively justifying the Keter classification. None of the effects listed or even obliquely hinted at seem to justify a classification higher than "Euclid". All we have justifying this thing's classification is the author's say-so and a throwaway reference to drastic measures needing to be taken in the case of a Stage Four or Stage Five outbreak. I may be in the wrong here, but it just strikes me as coming down on the wrong side of the line between "creepy and mysterious" and "obnoxiously obfuscated" as far as the justification for its class.

item.content:encoded: I haven't had a whole lot of time to properly revise this one (or anything else, for that matter), but I don't want to see it deleted, so a partial revision will have to do for now. I agree with cadence that part of 129's appeal is it could be out there, right now, so I'm thinking that should be played up. Maybe give Stage Three less obvious symptoms so it wouldn't look totally out of place in "the real world". Also, 129 can infect more than just people, so maybe an incident involving infected dogs, or cats, or bears….

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: We've got so many diseases and parasites that rely on creep-factor that I don't have any ideas on revitalizing this one. The unique thing it has going for it is that it resembles the modern cold at times, perhaps leading the reader to think "What if I've been infected?" It's an interesting idea but hard to carry out, and the execution here seems lacking. Any thoughts on how to expand on that?

item.content:encoded:
this is an intriguing article, but i have to note that .01% of 40% of humans equates to 240,000 of people currently living. that's a considerable number as far as diseases go and not something that would go unnoticed.

for comparison, fewer than 2000 cases of ebola have been reported since the discovery of the disease. heck, only 214 cases of mad cow disease in humans have come to light, and look at the level of panic that THAT'S given people.

i dont see how stage 3 with its rather distinctive symptoms would not have become common knowledge worldwide. or was this playing off of some disease i am simply unaware of?
